entries.originalText: Open, O Lord, my heart in Thy law, and teach me to walk in the way of Thy commandments.
entries.modernizedText: Open my heart, O Lord, in Your law, and teach me to walk in the way of Your commandments.

entries.originalText: Grant me to understand Thy will and to be mindful of Thy benefits, both general and special, with great reverence and diligent meditation, that thus I may be able worthily to give Thee thanks.
entries.modernizedText: Grant me to understand Your will and to be mindful of Your benefits, both general and special, with great reverence and diligent meditation, that thus I may be able worthily to give You thanks.

entries.originalText: Yet I know and confess that I cannot render Thee due praises for the least of Thy mercies.
entries.modernizedText: Yet I know and confess that I cannot render You due praises for the least of Your mercies.

entries.originalText: I am less than the least of all the good things which Thou gavest me; and when I consider Thy majesty, my spirit faileth because of the greatness thereof.
entries.modernizedText: I am less than the least of all the good things which You gave me; and when I consider Your majesty, my spirit fails because of its greatness.

entries.originalText: All things which we have in the soul and in the body, and whatsoever things we possess, whether outwardly or inwardly, naturally or supernaturally, are Thy good gifts, and prove Thee, from whom we have received them all, to be good, gentle, and kind.
entries.modernizedText: All things which we have in the soul and in the body, and whatever things we possess, whether outwardly or inwardly, naturally or supernaturally, are Your good gifts, and prove You, from whom we have received them all, to be good, gentle, and kind.

entries.originalText: Although one receiveth many things, and another fewer, yet all are Thine, and without Thee not even the least thing can be possessed.
entries.modernizedText: Although one receives many things, and another fewer, yet all are Yours, and without You not even the least thing can be possessed.

entries.originalText: He who hath received greater cannot boast that it is of his own merit, nor lift himself up above others, nor contemn those beneath him; for he is the greater and the better who ascribeth least to himself, and in giving thanks is the humbler and more devout; and he who holdeth himself to be viler than all, and judgeth himself to be the more unworthy, is the apter for receiving greater things.
entries.modernizedText: He who has received greater things cannot boast that it is of his own merit, or lift himself up above others, or despise those beneath him; for he is the greater and the better who ascribes least to himself, and in giving thanks is the humbler and more devout; and he who holds himself to be viler than all, and judges himself to be the more unworthy, is the more fit to receive greater things.

entries.originalText: But he who hath received fewer gifts, ought not to be cast down, nor to take it amiss, nor to envy him who is richer; but rather ought he to look unto Thee, and to greatly extol Thy goodness, for Thou pourest forth Thy gifts so richly, so freely and largely, without respect of persons.
entries.modernizedText: But he who has received fewer gifts ought not to be cast down, or take it amiss, or envy him who is richer; but rather he ought to look to You, and greatly extol Your goodness, for You pour forth Your gifts so richly, so freely and abundantly, without respect of persons.

entries.originalText: All things come of Thee; therefore in all things shalt thou be praised.
entries.modernizedText: All things come from You; therefore in all things You shall be praised.

entries.originalText: Thou knowest what is best to be given to each; and why this man hath less, and that more, is not for us but for Thee to understand, for unto Thee each man’s deservings are fully known.
entries.modernizedText: You know what is best to be given to each; and why this man has less, and that more, is not for us but for You to understand, for to You each man’s deservings are fully known.

entries.originalText: Wherefore, O Lord God, I reckon it even a great benefit, not to have many things, whence praise and glory may appear outwardly, and after the thought of men.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore, O Lord God, I reckon it even a great benefit not to have many things from which praise and glory may appear outwardly, and according to the thought of men.

entries.originalText: For so it is that he who considereth his own poverty and vileness, ought not only to draw therefrom no grief or sorrow, or sadness of spirit, but rather comfort and cheerfulness; because Thou, Lord, hast chosen the poor and humble, and those who are poor in this world, to be Thy friends and acquaintance.
entries.modernizedText: For so it is that he who considers his own poverty and vileness ought not only to draw from it no grief or sorrow or sadness of spirit, but rather comfort and cheerfulness; because You, Lord, have chosen the poor and humble, and those who are poor in this world, to be Your friends and acquaintances.

entries.originalText: So give all Thine apostles witness whom Thou hast made princes in all lands.
entries.modernizedText: So all Your apostles bear witness, whom You have made princes in all lands.

entries.originalText: Yet they had their conversation in this world blameless, so humble and meek, without any malice or deceit, that they even rejoiced to suffer rebukes for Thy Name’s sake,(1) and what things the world hateth, they embraced with great joy.
entries.modernizedText: Yet they lived in this world blameless, so humble and meek, without any malice or deceit, that they even rejoiced to suffer rebukes for Your Name’s sake,(1) and what things the world hates, they embraced with great joy.

entries.originalText: Therefore ought nothing so much to rejoice him who loveth Thee and knoweth Thy benefits, as Thy will in him, and the good pleasure of Thine eternal Providence, wherewith he ought to be so contented and comforted, that he would as willingly be the least as any other would be the greatest, as peaceable and contented in the lowest as in the highest place, and as willingly held of small and low account and of no name or reputation as to be more honourable and greater in the world than others.
entries.modernizedText: Therefore nothing ought so much to rejoice him who loves You and knows Your benefits as Your will in him, and the good pleasure of Your eternal Providence, with which he ought to be so contented and comforted that he would as willingly be the least as any other would be the greatest, as peaceable and contented in the lowest as in the highest place, and as willing to be held in small and low account and of no name or reputation as to be more honorable and greater in the world than others.

entries.originalText: For Thy will and the love of Thine honour ought to go before all things, and to please and comfort him more, than all benefits that are given or may be given to himself.
entries.modernizedText: For Your will and the love of Your honor ought to go before all things, and to please and comfort him more than all benefits that are given or may be given to himself.
